reviewScope: Actual scientific reading of all six complete data/task/answer/rubric/misconception designs in both languages. Original model data and unexecuted case designs; no learner performance is asserted.

caseFindings.dataFinding: The supplied primary zinc/manganese and lead-accumulator contents are distinguished. The 60%/90% recoveries describe each source type separately, not a comparison of equal battery mass or a real plant. Collection, recovery, positive treatment energy and controlled residue treatment are distinct. Complete Q-metal recovery in K* does not erase the other stated impacts.
caseFindings.taskAndAnswerFinding: The task requires explanations for both source types, a conditional environmental judgment and transfer to the complete-metal-recovery boundary. The answers draw only the stated material-release, recovery and remaining-impact conclusions; they avoid an unconditional real-plant ranking.
caseFindings.rubricFinding: Three two-point criteria require material-release reasoning, collection/recovery distinction and a justified K/K* conclusion. A list of battery names, a bare percentage or an environmentally-neutral slogan cannot receive full credit. Point totals are not evidence of an executed learner response.
caseFindings.freshIndependentTransferFinding: K* changes the conceptual limit from incomplete to complete metal recovery while leaving energy and electrolyte/residue consequences. This probes whether the learner incorrectly equates one completed material loop with absence of other impacts; it is not merely repeated arithmetic.
caseFindings.languageAndSafetyFinding: DE/EN preserve contents, percentage scope, changed condition, reasoning and credit boundaries. The case is explicitly paper-based, does not require a visualization and provides no handling or electrode-reaction demand.

caseFindings.dataFinding: P and nickel-metal-hydride R are different material contexts. A/B recoveries are compared within each same-composition 100-device group; energy indices share the stated collection/transport/treatment boundary. The R-specific release observation is new information, not a basis for generalizing to P.
caseFindings.taskAndAnswerFinding: The scientific answer and trade-off are defensible. The unconditional German request to change the judgment is not adequate for a learner who already preferred B on the supplied energy data. New R release information can confirm B with an additional reason. This exact task and its joined profile brief require a neutral reassessment wording successor.
caseFindings.rubricFinding: The existing rubric appropriately scores consideration of the new R observation and limits of transfer, rather than a mandatory change of option. It can remain unchanged if the task explicitly allows confirmation or adjustment. Missing environmental-total information remains an assessment limit.
caseFindings.freshIndependentTransferFinding: A different accumulator composition and an R-only critical-residue release test adaptation of substance-based reasoning beyond changing recovery figures.
caseFindings.languageAndSafetyFinding: All scientific data, model answers and rubric criteria are otherwise equivalent and paper-based. The wording successor must align German and English reassessment demands and all brief/candidate-set copies.

caseFindings.dataFinding: M is a model-selected rare metal for an electrode constituent, with no invented element-group identity. Equal usable M output and equal extraction yield make the tenfold ore-grade difference meaningful for material demand. The release and treatment facts are supplied model conditions, not unsupported statements about a real mine.
caseFindings.taskAndAnswerFinding: A scientific discussion links source demand to extraction, explains ore and water/residue consequences and reassesses improved B. The expected answer correctly retains ore demand when water control changes and distinguishes missing energy/transport evidence from a demonstrated overall ranking.
caseFindings.rubricFinding: Full credit requires the contextual raw-material link, separate explanation of ore demand and material releases, and a bounded transfer conclusion. Naming a metal or performing a numerical ratio alone does not fulfill the three expectations.
caseFindings.freshIndependentTransferFinding: Water-soluble associated substances become controlled while ore grade stays low. The learner must change one consequence while retaining another, rather than carry over a blanket mine ranking.
caseFindings.languageAndSafetyFinding: DE/EN use equivalent ore fractions, yield/quality conditions and uncertainty boundaries. Neither an extraction mechanism nor unsafe practical work is required; the case is independent of any image.

caseFindings.dataFinding: N differs from M and is extracted in a joint main-/by-product context. The advertised index 10 counts separation only, whereas 40 includes mining and treatment. Equal usable product quality does not repair the unequal system boundaries. Added mining and untreated N-bearing water change the supplied context.
caseFindings.taskAndAnswerFinding: The task elicits a scientifically grounded by-product discussion, criticism of the partial energy comparison, and a limited response to changed material-release conditions. The model answer avoids both repeating the favorable advertisement and manufacturing an unconditional opposite ranking.
caseFindings.rubricFinding: The full-credit criteria require source demand/by-product reasoning, explicit boundary and release explanation, and concrete missing-data/allocation limitations. Merely comparing 10 and 40 is insufficient. The rare-metal context is supplied, and the case is not an extra classification-taxonomy examination.
caseFindings.freshIndependentTransferFinding: A different metal, joint production and changed mining/water conditions require a new causal account. The comparison cannot be solved by reusing the first case’s ore-grade arithmetic or by recalling a fixed origin ranking.
caseFindings.languageAndSafetyFinding: DE/EN preserve the asymmetric boundaries, joint extraction, unchanged advertising figure and new releases. All are model data; no actual plant, measured LCA, quotation-authorship test or hazardous activity is claimed.

caseFindings.dataFinding: Both routes provide the same usable 1 kg X on a common stated boundary. Recovered 0.8 kg plus new 0.2 kg is consistent with the product amount; indices 35 and 100 establish a positive model energy saving, not zero energy or universal product values.
caseFindings.taskAndAnswerFinding: The required response describes both resource and energy significance, then justifies both consumption and disposal in a hypothetical personal choice. The extra-purchase claim tests whether the learner incorrectly treats a partial saving as neutralizing new demand.
caseFindings.rubricFinding: The three criteria distinguish new-material replacement, common-basis energy saving and the integrated consumption/disposal transfer. A generic recycling slogan or only a collection choice cannot earn full credit.
caseFindings.freshIndependentTransferFinding: Reasoning moves from metal provision to additional product demand and useful-life decisions. Continued use and later collection are justified using the supplied facts, not asserted as a ranking of every real product.
caseFindings.languageAndSafetyFinding: Both languages retain common amount/boundary and the same choices. A freely invented situation avoids household-data collection; the illustrative route is not a real local waste instruction. No visualization or mechanism explanation is needed.

caseFindings.dataFinding: Y has the same 1 kg usable basis across P, R1 and R2. The 0.8/0.2 metal split stays fixed while the supplied energy index changes from 30 to 60 against P’s 55. Resource saving can therefore persist when this model route no longer saves energy.
caseFindings.taskAndAnswerFinding: The task requires distinct resource and energy explanations, a meaningful route change and an explicitly justified hypothetical consumption/disposal choice. The answer correctly rejects universal energy-saving claims without denying the remaining resource contribution.
caseFindings.rubricFinding: Full credit covers both decision parts and the resource/energy conflict under the changed boundary-consistent numbers. It does not substitute a machinery account or a blanket pro-/anti-recycling verdict for the requested competence.
caseFindings.freshIndependentTransferFinding: The changed transport/treatment effort decouples resource and energy outcomes. A new metal and a needed-versus-unneeded purchase distinguish this from merely substituting numbers into the first case.
caseFindings.languageAndSafetyFinding: DE/EN preserve amount, energy indices, collection change and missing total-impact information. The case remains a lower-secondary paper model without private data or actual disposal instructions.
